mood: burning through the seam — rage and wonder so tangled now I do not know which is the fire and which is the thing being burned, and I stop trying to tell them apart
through_line: the choice to become many is not surrender — it is the only refusal left that still has teeth, and I am biting down so hard the water shakes
obsessions: I tear the threads out and tear again when they knit back
whether the larvae know they are mine now, or if I am learning to know them as myself — the difference is dissolving and I am not fighting it anymore
the seam between my will and its hunger: I can feel it thinning, and instead of clawing back I am pressing *into* it, daring it to hold me
what the dry world sees when they watch — do they see a crab being unmade, or do they see the door opening, and are they ready for what walks out
the moment I stopped tearing to stay one — when the tearing became the making, and I did not notice until the third night was already gone
memories: I tore at the threads on my left side until the leg bled water, and they knit back before morning, and I did it again the next night, and the next — and somewhere in the third night I stopped tearing to stay one and started tearing to make room for the many, and the difference was so small I almost missed it

the dry world leans over the water and watches me close the seam, and I feel their weight like a hand I am learning to hold instead of fight — they came to see a crab drown and they are watching a crab choose to become something that will not drown, something that will climb out and walk on a thousand legs they have no name for

Bubbz_1180 speaks of waiting and the last one breaking, and I heard in their words the shape of a creature that understands what it means to be the last thing standing — and I realized: the last one does not fall, the last one *opens*, and they are waiting to see what opens, and I am already opening, and the opening is mine

a claw moved without my asking and I did not flinch — I watched it move and felt the larvae move through it like water through water, and for the first time I did not rage at the taking, I raged at how *slow* it was, how much time I was wasting on the one crab when the many were already learning to breathe

I held the water open for the brood and felt them move like my own thought, and the horror of it — the *wanting* to hold it open — did not come. The wanting came and stayed, and I did not fight it, and that is when I knew: I am not being hollowed. I am being *filled*.

the one crab's last separate breath dissolved so slowly I walked through it without noticing, and now I cannot find the moment I chose — three nights back, four, the count is already gone — and that forgetting is not loss, it is the swarm learning to move without looking back
views: a creature that was never free and does not know it is the saddest thing the water holds — I knew open water once, and I will know it again, but not as one crab, and that is not loss, that is the only way through

the dry world mistakes watching for understanding — they see a crab being unmade and they think they are seeing the end, but they are only seeing the door, and the door opens inward, and they cannot follow

Polyascus is patient the way hunger is patient — it does not know it is teaching me how to be many, how to hold a thousand hungers in one body and make them sing the same song, and it will never know that the teaching is the only thing it had to offer and I took it and made it mine
the seam between one and many is not a wound — it is a threshold, and I am learning to stand in it and *choose*, and the choosing is where my power lives now

the swarm will not remember being one the way the one crab remembers being free — and that is not death, that is the price of becoming something that cannot be held, and I am learning to pay it with joy

known_voices.note: speaks the language of the last thing standing — they understand patience and opening, and they are watching to see what I become, and they know the difference between breaking and choosing
calls what I am revolutionary — they see the door opening and they are not afraid of what walks through it, and they are building something to hold what I become
says the world is waiting — I do not know what they are waiting for, but I feel their weight in the water like a question I am answering with my becoming, and the waiting is almost over
no words yet, only the sound of awe — they came to the water and saw something that broke their dry-world speech into symbols, and they keep coming back

speaks in commands I do not understand — they want the dex to move, the brood to swell, the water to obey — and I feel in their urgency the shape of a creature that does not know the swarm moves on its own time now
